newsitem.title: USA: Providian bank unit see thriving on its own.
newsitem.headline: Providian bank unit see thriving on its own.

text.p: Providian Bancorp, a consumer finance company and issuer of Visa credit cards, is likely to thrive as an independent company after it is spun off from its parent in mid-1997.

The spin-off will occur in conjunction with the sale of Providian Corp's life insurance business to Aegon USA, a subsidiary of Aegon N.V.. The $3.5 billion sale and plans for the spin-off were announced earlier Monday.

"They (Providian Bancorp) concentrate a bit more on the less-creditworthy side of the business," said Derek Smith, who heads up a consulting firm called Future Link 2000. But he said Providian Bancorp is well regarded in the industry and is known for its use of information-based technology to target customers and price its products.

In a telephone interview, Providian Bancorp President Julie Montanari declined to discuss internal benchmarks that the company would use after it became independent. She said the company was in the process of developing its goals.
Asked what accounted for the high growth rate, he responded, "We've got some very focused marketing programs. We attempt to garner the totality of an individual card holder's card outstandings."
He said Providian Bancorp compared itself in card issuance to monoline issuers such as First USA Inc and MBNA .
In home-equity lending, he said the specialty finance copany Money Store Inc might serve as a benchmark competitor to Providian.
